brief: Saudi Arabia's October oil output hit 10.6mb/d, up 27% MoM and near pre-war levels, helping explain sub-$4 gasoline; risks remain from the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks, and the 12-month WTI target of $65 depends on a US-Iran deal. MBA's 30-year mortgage rate fell a fourth straight week to 7.21%, but it is still ~90bps higher YTD, applications remain near a 2025 low, and existing home sales data today is unlikely to bring real relief. US data is beating forecasts while Europe's is missing, and with a hawkish Fed this has pushed the dollar to a 20-month high; the firm expects fewer Fed hikes than markets price, calling the dollar rally stretched, yet still prefers US equities on relative growth. Anthropic's IPO, targeting up to $1.5t and reportedly oversubscribed, is seen reviving AI sentiment after post-election jitters, reinforcing a positive Tech call (2027 EPS growth 42% vs 16% for the S&P 500). Separately, BofA data shows auction-house art sales up ~70% YoY to $6.8b in 1H26, the strongest since 2022, though the piece notes art's value, like crypto and gold, is sentiment-driven.
